title: Vetala Story 14: The Man Who Transmigrated
summary: The Vetala whispered: 'Hearken, King, to the mystery of the Transmigrated Yogi!'...
keywords: vetala story 14: the man who transmigrated
full_text:
Under the dark sky, King Vikramaditya hauled the corpse back across his shoulders.

The Vetala whispered: 'Hearken, King, to the mystery of the Transmigrated Yogi!'

In the Himalayas lived a young yogi named Devadatta who mastered the occult art of transferring his living soul into dead bodies.

While walking through the forest, he saw the young, handsome King of Kosala fall dead from his stallion during a hunt. Knowing the queen and kingdom would be plunged into despair, the yogi transferred his soul into the dead king's body, while leaving his own ascetic body hidden in a mountain cave.

Animating the royal frame, the yogi-king returned to the capital, ruled with extraordinary justice, relieved taxes, and comforted the grieving queen.

Meanwhile, a wandering shepherd found the yogi's abandoned, lifeless human body in the cave, believed it was a corpse, and burned it on a funeral pyre according to custom!

When the yogi wished to return to his ascetic life, his own body was ashes; he was permanently trapped in the body of the King!

Here the Vetala asked: 'Tell me, King Vikramaditya: was this yogi a saint who sacrificed his spiritual liberation to govern a kingdom, or a usurper who stole another's throne? Answer, or your head will shatter!'

Vikramaditya answered: 'He was a noble soul who performed a supreme act of selfless sacrifice. He gained no worldly pleasure, for his mind remained detached in ascetic wisdom; but he saved a kingdom from civil war and governed for the welfare of millions, surrendering his own physical identity for the dharma of the realm.'

'Justly resolved!' chuckled the Vetala, and flew back to his tree.
moral: The soul that abandons its appointed duty to inhabit another's glory reaps spiritual vacancy.
